chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:

Regarding a man who swore an oath that he would not speak to any of his relatives, he said: It is not binding, so let him speak to the one he swore against. And he said: Every oath in which the Face of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is not intended, is not binding regarding divorce or manumission.

He said: And I asked him about a woman who dedicated her wealth as a Hadi (sacrificial animal/gift) for the House of Allah, if she lent her belongings to So-and-so and So-and-so, and some of her family lent them without her command. He said: There is no Hadi upon her. Rather, the Hadi is what is dedicated for Allah as a Hadi for the Kaaba; that is what is fulfilled when dedicated for Allah. And whatever is similar to this is not binding, nor a Hadi, if Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is not mentioned in it.
And he was asked about a man who says, 'Upon me is a thousand camels,' and he is in Ihram for a thousand Hajjs. He said: That is from the footsteps of Satan.

And regarding a man who says, and he is in Ihram for a Hajj, he said: It is not binding. Or he says, 'I gift this food,' he said: It is not binding. Indeed, food is not gifted as a Hadi. Or he says, 'The carcass, after it has been slaughtered, I gift it for the House of Allah,' he said: Rather, the camels are gifted while they are alive, and they are not gifted when they have become meat.

key_terms.مُحْرِم: One in the state of Ihram (pilgrimal consecration)

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for an oath or vow to be binding in Shia fiqh, and what constitutes a valid Hadi sacrifice?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the principle of 'Yamin al-Ghaws' (excessive or casual oaths) by establishing that oaths lacking sincere intent for Allah's sake are not binding, a key concept in Shia fiqh for distinguishing between binding vows and casual speech. It further refines the jurisprudence of Hadi (sacrificial gift) by specifying that valid offerings must be living animals dedicated specifically to the Kaaba, thereby excluding general gifts or slaughtered meat from this category. These rulings highlight the Shia emphasis on intentionality (niyyah) and precise textual criteria in ritual obligations.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said regarding a man who swore an oath that he would not speak to the relatives of his’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is not with anything. So let him speak to the ones he had sworn against’. And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Every oath, not intending by it the Face of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic, so it is not with anything, regarding a divorce, or freeing a slave’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a woman who made her wealth to be a gift for the House of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, if she lends her belongings to so and so, and so and so, so some of her family lend these without her instructions. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no sacrifice upon her. But rather, the sacrifice is what she made for the sake of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> as a gift for the Kaaba. So that is what needs to be fulfilled with, when it is made for the Sake of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>; and whatever was resembling from this, so is not with anything, nor a sacrifice not mentioning Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic in it’.
And I asked himasws about the man saying, ‘Upon me are a thousand camels’, and he is in Ihraam, ‘along with a thousand Hajj’. Heasws said: ‘That is from the footsteps of Satanla’.

And about the man who is saying, and he is in Ihraam with the Hajj?’ Heasws said: ‘It is not with anything’. (I said), ‘Or he is saying, ‘I hereby gift this food?’ Heasws: ‘It is not with anything. The food cannot be a sacrifice’. (I said), ‘Or is saying, ‘The camels, after having been slaughtered, it is to be gifted with for the House of Allahazwj’. Heasws said: ‘But rather, the camel is sacrificed when these are alive, and it is not gifted when it becomes meat’.
en.sarwar: 12. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has narrated the following:

“About the case of a man who takes an oath not to speak to a certain relative, abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘It does not have any valid effect. He must speak to one about whom he has taken an oath not to speak.’ He (the Imam) then said, ‘Any oath which is not for the sake of Allah does not have any valid effect, whether it is in divorce or freeing a slave.’

He (the narrator) has said, ‘I then asked him (the Imam) about a woman who has made her assets for the house of Allah if certain woman borrows her certain items and also so and so woman, then certain ones allow her to borrow and others do not allow.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘There is an offering animal on her. Offering is what Allah has made a gift for al-Ka’bah and for this reason it is offered if it is made for Allah. Such things are of no valid effect as well as such offering animal on which Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, is not mentioned.’

He (the Imam) was asked about a man who says that there are one thousand camels on me when he is in the state of Ihram, or a thousand al-Hajj. He (the Imam) said, ‘Such things are of the temptation of Satan.’

About the case of a man who in the state of Ihram takes an oath for al-Hajj or that he says to offer this food. He (the Imam) said, ‘It does not have any valid effect.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It does not have any valid effect; food cannot be offered. He may say that the camel slaughtered after it is slaughtered, he wants to offer it to the house of Allah.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Camels are offered when they are living, not when it turns to flesh.’”
